pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds a NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK column; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are all 0 and that 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list with ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and asserts id order of only starred items, status 200.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give all items in id order.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty, __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards prototype keys.
traffic/routes.json includes /?show=starred; 'AC-7' test asserts it; checker script was updated to accept query strings.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits') deleted the 'Empty table' state test, which checked the empty message and the 'Starred only' link. The only remaining empty-table test (test/index.test.js:30) checks the message but not the link. The spec's state row 'Empty table' (No items yet. + link to Starred only) is therefore only partly covered. The link is untested for that state. The commit also left a stray double blank line.
findings.fix:
Restore the deleted test (delete all items, expect no
  • , 'No items yet.', and the 'Starred only' link).

findings.what: The PR body says test/starred.test.js covers 'each state'. The Empty table state is not fully covered after the final commit. The body says 'Tests deleted: none', but the final commit deletes a test it added earlier in the same change.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or correct the PR claim.

lenses.note: The spec exists and its decisions are followed: starred items keep their id order, and the view is a query parameter.
All 7 ACs are named by tests. The Empty table state row is only partly tested; see the finding.
I did not run the tests; CI runs them. The Empty table state test was removed in the final commit.
The SQL uses fixed fragments from a whitelist, and Object.hasOwn rejects prototype keys. No defect found.
The show param is whitelisted and titles are escaped. The traffic route checker still refuses spaces and #.
The change only adds a link and a ★ in plain HTML, with no UI files or styles.
The change has no browser-visible UI beyond plain HTML, and no screenshots exist.
The 'each state covered' and 'tests deleted: none' claims are not fully accurate; see the finding.
